source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Allen campus publishes 77 MW of IT capacity across three facilities, making it the second-largest by power in Texas and representing 16 percent of all published state capacity.

At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this translates to roughly 1,925 racks. The concentration of that much power in one operator and region matters for AI scaling because GPU training workloads are power-dense and spatially fixed. A single campus cannot move if its grid connection is exhausted. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities overall, but only 19 publish power figures. The Allen campus is visible; most of the state is not.

The facility holds certifications for regulated workloads in payments, healthcare, federal systems, and information security. These designations constrain how operators can use the space and may reduce available capacity for commercial AI training, though the data does not specify utilization by workload type.

Critical gaps prevent assessment of whether this campus constrains or enables AI deployment. The operator does not publish total power consumption, PUE, grid interconnection capacity, water usage, or power source composition. Without those figures, the campus cannot be read as grid-constrained or grid-available. AI scaling impact depends on grid supply, not IT load alone.
